parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is the governing state's national law applied to the island with no departmental variation. Documented exposures: visitors who enter detention are placed by legal sex, with a 2021 detention-watchdog report documenting serious, persistent violations against transgender detainees — a tier-1 custody exposure corroborated (not remedied) by recurring oversight findings. Documented protections are resident-facing or thin: a penal-code discrimination ground covering transphobia (recourse exists on paper, but no documented visitor-facing enforcement), and LGR/marriage machinery that is climate signal only. No criminalisation of gender expression is documented. The custody exposure governs the worst case; everyday border, facility and street treatment is undocumented, not evidenced safe. Sits in Elevated Risk, mid-band: above pure-birth-sex-custody anchors thanks to documented anti-discrimination law, below Reduced-Risk anchors because no working remedy for documented custodial harm is shown.

entry_documents.protection: National document rules apply; no visitor-specific border friction or accommodation documented either way.
entry_documents.interaction: Border encounter would run under national rules with no island layer.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Trans women imprisoned by legal-sex assignment under national rules applicable here; 2021 watchdog report documents serious persistent violations against trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented as operative for detainees; recurring findings show unremedied practice.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or immigration hold escalates into birth-sex custody exposure under national custodial rules.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Custodial placement by legal sex is the documented facility exposure; hospital-ward practice not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National ministries and courts operate directly on the island.

care_services.interaction: National healthcare framework applies; island provision unevidenced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Not documented as targeting trans visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Sexual identity is a penal-code discrimination ground, enabling prosecution of transphobia — a documented recourse pathway, not shown operating.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National enforcement and prosecution apply directly.

minors_guardians.exposure: Same custodial and document exposure would apply to a travelling minor via national rules; no department-specific documentation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardians encounter the same national regime; nothing island-specific.

street_violence_police_response.protection: Discrimination ground provides theoretical recourse; no documented enforcement record.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response would follow national practice; island practice unevidenced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unknowns: local enforcement character, border practice, healthcare access, street climate on the island — thin inventory, extrapolated from national structural record.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Penal-code ground and LGR machinery are documented national climate signals; not credited as visitor protections.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Watchdog findings recurring without remedy indicate oversight does not currently fix custodial exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar core exposure: birth/legal-sex prison placement with harm to detainees. Here no cross-dressing statute is documented, and a penal-code discrimination ground plus documented LGR climate exist; those push modestly above 0.25-C, though recurring unremedied custodial violations keep the deduction substantial.

Comparable tier: durable structural exposure (custody/registration-style) with weak oversight — ombuds/monitor findings that do not remedy. This dossier's custody exposure is more severe (documented detainee harm) but narrower in reach than 0.45-D's universal registration; net position is close, slightly higher due to documented anti-discrimination law.

Below 0.75-C: that anchor shows remedies actually working (counsel, compensation, tribunal relief) and no documented custodial placement exposure. This dossier documents persistent custodial violations with no shown working remedy, holding it a full band lower.

Above 0.35-C: that anchor's reporting regime reaches every visitor continuously with eviction and fines. Here the documented universal exposure is limited to the detention pathway, not everyday lodging or travel, and a discrimination ground exists on paper.

parsed.synthesis: The island adds no legal layer of its own; the operative regime is the governing state's national framework. Its worst documented feature is tier-1-adjacent: legal-sex imprisonment placement with a 2021 watchdog report of serious persistent violations — recurring findings corroborate an unremedied exposure rather than mitigating it. Against this stand a penal-code discrimination ground enabling transphobia prosecution (documented but not shown operating for visitors) and resident-facing LGR/marriage machinery counted only as climate. Everyday border, facility, care and street experience is undocumented; thin-data extrapolation from the national record (functioning institutions, anti-discrimination statute, no expression criminalisation, but custodial failure) resolves to mid Elevated Risk. The custodial pathway dominates the worst case; the discrimination ground and absence of expression laws keep it above the 0.25 tier.
